original.description: Objective: To derive a standard set of requirements for the ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) Security Module and implement a prototype form-factor equivalent ADHA module.Description: The ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) has been initiated through a collaboration between ESA, European satellite primes and data handling equipment suppliers. The initiative has resulted in the agreement on an architecture for data handling unit based on standard module functions. A standard module procurement flow has been defined, as well as a standardized backplane connector and electrical interfaces. This allows independent development of interoperable modules that can be connected together in ADHA units. More advanced security functions are expected to be required in future ESA missions. The modular format of the proposed solution will enable faster adoption, and verification of new security technologies, in different unit configurations. This activity aims to perform analysis work to derive a standardization of the security function within an ADHA module form-factor, to allow the development of ADHA-compliant security products, which can be utilized together with other existing ADHA products, such as ADHA OBC. When implemented in the ADHA 3U form factor, such units are of particular interest for use in mid-size satellite platforms as well (less than 500kg mass). For prototyping purposes, the target of this activity is an elegant breadboard (EBB) of the ADHA security module in 6U format, based on the security function requirements defined in this activity. The extended format will provide the required design margins for the prototyping and demonstration phase. The long-term goal, this technology development, is the adaptation of this security module to an ADHA 3U module form factor. This activity encompasses thefollowing tasks: - Analyse the use-cases for dedicated security modules in data handling systems, both for platform and payload - Derive the detailed generic requirements for ADHA Security Modules, including functions, performances, electrical and software interfaces, etc. and present the specifications for review of the ADHA consortia and industrial working group - Derive the architectural design of a prototype ADHA Security Module - Derive a prototype electrical and software design of an ADHA Security Module, as an EBB in ADHA 6U format. - Perform functional validation of the prototype and demonstrate a representative use-case for the ADHA Security Module - Derive a roadmap for bringing the derived design to an ADHA 3U security module EM/EQM/FM.

original.description: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a power module that will be integrated in an autonomous spacecraftarchitecture.Targeted  Improvements:Increase the level of onboard autonomy by 50% at overall platform level.Description: Current satellite operations require human intervention from ground, resulting in considerable inefficiencies and dependencies on communication window frequency, latency, and available resources, which become more prominent for large constellations. This activity aims to partially remove the current dependence of the spacecraft on ground stations by developing an intelligent power module for an autonomous satellite, based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) to autonomously process and interpret housekeeping and telemetry data and take decisions on needed actions in real-time. This is essential for management of future constellations. Current power subsystems canautonomously power up the system, however, for future autonomous satcom satellites, the FDIR (Failure Detection, Identification, and Recovery) system's capability to provide failure prognostics are crucial for the satellite autonomy especially in unforeseen circumstances. This is a very complicated technical issue that the traditional methods cannot cope with, thus, a new approach shall be developed targeting an autonomous system, based on AI, implementing health monitoring blocks in the power module, and interacting withthe rest of the satellite, identifying in advance performance drift, preventing failures and keeping the power system operational in any flight circumstance. The concept is to train an AI system to identify combinations of housekeeping telemetry data series thatexhibit non nominal behaviours and take the right decision accordingly.The activity will develop an architecture for a power modulefor autonomous satellites. Primary functions to be autonomously implemented by the module will be trade-off taking resource requirements into consideration. Parameters, format and the commands to be generated will be identified, and the unit's management strategywill be developed.Finally, the algorithms needed to monitor the health and performance status, drifts and failure prognostics willbe designed. A breadboard model of the power module will be designed, manufactured and experimentally tested to evaluate the developed concepts and algorithms and achieved autonomy.

original.description: Objective: The objective is to design, develop and test an Automatic Identification System (AIS) spoofing detection system onboard the satellite for satellite-based maritime surveillance, offeringreliable AIS information with low-latency.TargetedImprovements: Reduce by half the latency of detection of non-reliable reporting vessels compared to current technologies. Decrease reliance on ground-based infrastructures by enabling onboarddetection of deceptive AIS signals.Description: With approximately 90% of international trade travelling by sea, maritime routes are becoming increasingly congested. A reliable maritime domain awareness is thus paramount toaddress critical security (e.g. submarine cables, piracy), safety (e.g. collision avoidance), economic (e.g. fleet monitoring) or environmental (e.g. illegal fishing) needs, and space-basedcomponents are critical due to the limited terrestrial systems coverage. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is one of the main components of the current maritime domain awarenessinfrastructure, being mandated by International Maritime Organisation and enabling the reporting of vessels worldwide. However, the current AIS setup suffers from reliability issues.Vessels can arbitrarily either switch off their AIS transponder or use (or being the target of) malicious deceiving techniques such as AIS spoofing and jamming or manipulation of GNSSinformation embedded in such messages. This results in fictitious abnormal behaviours that are becoming increasingly common and causing significant disruption across entire regions.Moreover, traditional satellite-based AIS processing systems rely heavily on ground-based validation, leading to high latency in spoofing detection and reducing the effectiveness of real timecountermeasures.An onboard detection module could overcome these challenges by detecting in near real-time any AIS anomaly and initiate the mitigation countermeasures, i.e. paired with communicationto other trailing satellites or direct-to-device communication links (out of the scope of this activity), such detection system could inform users about fraudulent activities faster thantraditional surveillance systems.This activity will develop and test an onboard Automatic Identification System (AIS) spoofing detection system for satellite-based maritime surveillance, offering reliableAIS informationwith low-latency. Low latency AI-based anomaly detection and other technologies such as signal fingerprinting and deterministic algorithms will be investigated and developed.The AIS spoofing detection module shall be designed according to selecteduse cases and implemented on a software-defined radio-based payload and tested in a representativemaritime surveillance scenario to evaluate its effectiveness in detecting, localising, and mitigating AIS spoofing in real time.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required.
